def: An open protocol, now under the Linux Foundation, for one agent to discover, delegate work to and receive results from another agent without seeing its internals.
A peer agent whose model, prompts, tools and memory are hidden from its caller, which sees only its card, messages, tasks and artifacts.
A JSON document in which an agent describes its name, interfaces, capabilities, security requirements and skills, so clients can discover and call it.
An entry in an agent card describing one capability of the agent, with an id, description, tags and examples.
A stateful unit of work with an id, a context, a status and artifacts, which a client can poll, cancel or resume.
The lifecycle position of an A2A task: submitted, working, input-required or auth-required while active, and completed, failed, canceled or rejected once finished.
An output of an A2A task, made of parts such as text, a file or structured data, as distinct from the messages of the conversation.
An identifier that groups related A2A messages and tasks into one conversation so follow-ups can refer to earlier work.
A task state (completed, failed, canceled or rejected) from which an A2A task cannot be restarted; changes are made in a new task in the same context.
A webhook call that an A2A server makes to a client-registered URL when a long-running task changes, sparing the client from polling.
Signing a canonicalised agent card with a JSON Web Signature so a client can verify its publisher and detect alteration.
